steps: A star topology is easy to install and manage because each computer is connected directly to a central hub or switch.
If one cable or computer fails, the other computers on the network continue to work.
Faults can be detected and isolated easily because each connection is separate.
New computers can be added to the network without interrupting the other computers.
Data travels through the central hub or switch, which helps manage communication on the network.
items.finalAnswer: Star topology is easy to manage, troubleshoot, and expand, and a failure in one connection does not normally affect the rest of the network.

steps: A firewall is a hardware device or software that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic.
It checks network traffic against security rules and blocks unauthorised access.
It helps protect computers and networks from hackers, malicious software, and other network threats.
A firewall allows legitimate communication while restricting suspicious or unwanted traffic.
items.finalAnswer: A firewall protects a network by checking traffic and blocking unauthorised or suspicious access.

steps: Computer networks are used to share resources, such as printers, storage devices, software, and an internet connection.
For example, several computers in an office can use the same network printer and shared files.
Networks enable data communication between connected computers and devices.
Users can send messages, transfer files, and exchange information over a network.
For example, email and video calls allow people in different places to communicate quickly.
items.finalAnswer: Computer networks enable resource sharing and fast data communication between connected devices.

steps: Given: Data rate = 500 bits per second (bps); message size = 10 kilobits = 10,000 bits.
Required: Time to transmit the message.
Formula: Time = Data size ÷ Data rate.
Substitution: Time = 10,000 bits ÷ 500 bits per second.
Working: Time = 20 seconds.
Result: The message takes 20 seconds to transmit.
Given: Data rate = 500 bits per second (bps); message size = 10 kilobytes = 10 × 1,024 bytes = 10,240 bytes.
Convert to bits: 10,240 bytes × 8 bits per byte = 81,920 bits.
Required: Time to transmit the message.
Formula: Time = Data size ÷ Data rate.
Substitution: Time = 81,920 bits ÷ 500 bits per second.
Working: Time = 163.84 seconds.
Result: The message takes 163.84 seconds to transmit.
In packet switching, a message is divided into small units called packets.
Each packet may travel independently through the network using an available route.
The packets are reassembled in the correct order at the destination.
Packet switching uses network resources efficiently, but packets may take different routes or arrive at different times.
In circuit switching, a dedicated communication path is established between the sender and receiver before data is sent.
The path remains reserved for the duration of the communication and is released when the communication ends.
Circuit switching provides a continuous connection, but the reserved path cannot be used by others during that time.
items.finalAnswer: Packet switching sends separate packets that are reassembled at the destination, while circuit switching reserves a dedicated path for the communication.

steps: Protocols are rules that define how data is formatted, transmitted, received, and interpreted in a network.
They allow devices and software from different sources to communicate correctly.
TCP/IP is a suite of protocols used for communication over the Internet; IP addresses and routes data, while TCP helps deliver it reliably.
HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer web pages and other web resources between a web server and a browser.
DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns network settings, including IP addresses, to devices joining a network.
items.finalAnswer: Protocols make network communication possible; TCP/IP transfers data, HTTP transfers web resources, DNS finds IP addresses for domain names, and DHCP assigns network settings.

steps: A firewall monitors network traffic and blocks unauthorised or suspicious connections; it helps prevent unwanted access to a network.
Encryption converts readable data into coded form so that unauthorised people cannot understand it; the data can be read by someone with the correct key.
Antivirus software detects, blocks, and removes viruses and other malicious software from a computer.
These methods protect against different threats and are most effective when used together and kept up to date.
Security methods reduce risk, but users should also use strong passwords and avoid suspicious files and links.
items.finalAnswer: Firewalls control network access, encryption protects the privacy of data, and antivirus software detects and removes malware; using them together provides stronger security.
